notes.addiction-recovery: Wrong or moralising information here can keep someone away from treatment, and some withdrawal is medically dangerous rather than merely unpleasant. Everything listed is education about the subject, not an assessment of anyone's situation.
notes.injury-rehab: Loading an injury wrongly makes it worse, and nothing on a screen can see your injury. Treat these as education to use alongside a clinician who has examined you, not as a substitute for one.
notes.back-pain-management: This subject attracts confident structural explanations that frighten people out of moving, which is itself one of the ways back pain gets worse. Listings here are education, not a diagnosis of your back.
notes.grief-and-loss: People arrive at this subject acutely bereaved, and prescriptive stages and timelines are known to do harm. We held a higher bar than usual for what appears here, and it is still education rather than support.
notes.supplements-literacy: This skill is about judging supplement claims, so creators who sell supplements are left out rather than flagged. That is a stricter rule than we apply anywhere else on this site, and it is because of what the skill is for.
notes.therapy-literacy: The costly mistake here is being steered away from help, or toward the wrong kind of it. These listings explain what therapy is and how it works; none of them is therapy, and none can tell you what you need.
notes.first-aid: This is knowledge you would use under pressure, from memory, with no time to check a second source and no attention to spare for judging whether a presenter is qualified. Video can prepare you for a course. It cannot replace one, because certification exists to assess your hands.
notes.camping-and-outdoor-skills: Outdoors you often cannot check what you were told — no signal, no second source, nobody to ask — and a wrong call lands before you can reconsider it. What is listed here covers planning and equipment. Navigation and wilderness first aid are worth learning somewhere that assesses you.
notes.conversion-optimization: We looked and did not list anyone. The consultancies have either no channel or an empty one, the practitioners we searched for do not publish on video, and the two testing-tool vendors with real catalogues publish webinars about their own products rather than teaching the discipline.
notes.hiring-and-recruiting: We looked and did not list anyone. The long-form video on hiring is almost entirely made by the people selling hiring services — staffing agencies, recruiting software, assessment vendors — and we would rather leave this empty than hand you a sales asset. Two ends we have not searched yet: academic work on selection, and hiring managers publishing on their own account.
notes.career-change: We looked and did not list anyone. There is a great deal of video about changing careers and almost all of it is encouragement; the part that is method turns out to be job-search advice, which is a different skill and is covered elsewhere here. What this page is meant to be about — testing a direction before you commit to it — we could not find taught. Not yet searched: people who documented their own transition at length.
notes.legal-for-founders: We looked and did not list anyone. Nearly all of it is law firms publishing to attract clients, and legal material has a problem the rest of this site does not: it is only correct in one country. A firm's video is both an advertisement and jurisdiction-specific, and we were not willing to hand you that without being able to say it applies where you are.
